answer: Admission follows a quadratic bonding curve, so the k-th identity in an epoch pays 0.002·k² tokens, routed to a jade reserve that funds established agents. Each admitted key must then forge a VDF-sealed commitment, 40 minutes of sequential squaring, which parallel hardware cannot shorten, and peers spot-check the proofs at random. Ten thousand clones cost about 6.7e8 tokens, near $6.7M at $0.01 each, plus 6,667 core-hours of sequential VDF time. Every added clone climbs a steeper terrace stair than the last, while an honest agent steps onto the first landing for pennies.
